question: Should OpenClaw add first-party per-agent backup/restore/clone, and what exact state is portable across credentials, transcripts, workspace files, config entries, and agent SQLite databases?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose credential/session portability, destructive restore behavior, or coordination with the broader snapshot restore work without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design first-party per-agent recovery
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-owned design before implementation covering archive format, secret policy, transcript policy, rollback, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Defer behind snapshot restore
options.body: Wait for the broader encrypted snapshot restore work to land before defining the narrower per-agent clone layer.

options.title: Decline core clone command
options.body: Close this direction and document manual/plugin-owned approaches if maintainers decide per-agent clone is not a core backup responsibility.

recommendation.title: Design first-party per-agent recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-owned design before implementation covering archive format, secret policy, transcript policy, rollback, and upgrade compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup, auth persistence, and SQLite state work makes this the best available owner for the remaining product/security choice.
